short: A German light cruiser that waged a highly successful independent raiding campaign across the Indian Ocean in 1914.
full:
Commissioned into the Imperial German Navy on 10 July 1909, SMS Emden was a light cruiser assigned to the East Asia Squadron based at Tsingtao. At the outbreak of the First World War, rather than retreating with the main squadron, her commander Karl von Müller took her on an independent commerce-raiding cruise into the Indian Ocean. 

For three months, Emden terrorised Allied shipping. She captured or sank over two dozen merchant vessels, bombarded Madras, and audaciously attacked the harbour at Penang, sinking a Russian cruiser and a French destroyer. Her crew gained widespread admiration for their chivalrous treatment of captured sailors. Her reign ended on 9 November 1914 at the Battle of Cocos, where she was intercepted and severely battered by the Australian cruiser HMAS Sydney, forcing her to run aground.
